proof_0481.moves: Both sides unfold to the same search over the slice, so the equality of contains-with-a-Char-pattern and contains-with-the-(· == c)-predicate holds definitionally; the proof is rfl.

proof_0482.moves: A component complement is contained in its image under hom, and a set containing an infinite set is infinite; so apply monotonicity of Set.Infinite to subset_hom.

proof_0483.moves: Turn the ring homs into algebra structures, note the composite gives a scalar tower (algebraMap equality holds by rfl), then descend formal etaleness along restriction of scalars.

proof_0484.moves: Membership in the closure means membership in every non-unital subsemiring containing s, so any element of s qualifies; apply the mpr direction of mem_closure.

proof_0485.moves: The plausible-successor relation is defined as the stated inverse image, so the two sides are definitionally equal; the proof is rfl.

proof_0486.moves: The theory-level iff formula is equivalent to the conjunction of the two implications; take the right conjunct of that equivalence.

proof_0487.moves: Pairwise with the bottom relation says no two distinct points of s are related at all, which is exactly subsingleton-ness; apply the forward direction of pairwise_bot_iff.

proof_0488.moves: Reduce a = ⊤ to ⊤ ≤ a via eq_top_iff, then feed codisjointness the two bounds a ≤ a (reflexivity) and b ≤ a.

proof_0489.moves: Construct the isometric-action instance for the additive opposite: the opposite action is the original action by the unopped element, so the extended distance is unchanged by edist_vadd_left.

proof_0490.moves: Chain two known bridges: the implementation's minEntry? agrees with the model version minEntry?ₘ, which in turn agrees with the list-level minEntry? on the tree's list model, using the ordering invariant.

proof_0491.moves: Write Ico a b as the intersection Iio b ∩ Ici a, then use that Iio is locally closed (open) and Ici is locally closed (closed) together with closure of local closedness under intersection.

proof_0492.moves: The subfield attached to an intermediate field has the same underlying carrier, so the two membership statements are definitionally the same; the proof is Iff.rfl.

proof_0493.moves: Destructure the arrays as wrappers around lists, transport the permutation to the underlying lists, and apply List.Perm.mem_iff, rewriting array membership as list membership.

proof_0494.moves: Iio is injective on a linear order, and an injective function's equality of values is equivalent to equality of arguments.

proof_0495.moves: Case-split the integer argument into the nonneg (cast of a nat) and negSucc branches; in each branch the Nonnegg predicate reduces definitionally to the claimed SqLe statement or to True.

proof_0496.moves: Unpack the raw tree map's well-formedness to get the invariant on the inner implementation, then apply the implementation-level get!_erase! lemma.

proof_0497.moves: In a normal space every neighbourhood of a set contains a closed neighbourhood of it; feed that existence statement to the self-basis criterion for filters to get a basis of closed neighbourhoods.

proof_0498.moves: Given the edge from the start to v and v on the path's support, compare the single-edge path u→v with the truncation of p up to v; in an acyclic graph paths between two vertices are unique (Subsingleton), so the two agree and v must be p.snd.

proof_0499.moves: Assemble the equivalence-relation structure from the three already-proved facts: reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity of the right-fraction relation (the calculus of fractions hypothesis is what makes transitivity available).

proof_0500.moves: The claim that a set is contained in the von Neumann ordinal of its own rank; here it is discharged by simp-generated rewriting that reduces the goal to reflexivity of ≤ on ordinals, with the actual content buried in a private simp lemma.

proof_0501.moves: Rewrite subtraction as addition of the negation, then rewrite negation as multiplication by -1 and identify -1 with the appropriate UInt8 literal; a chain of rewrites.

proof_0502.moves: Translate each congruence into a divisibility of the difference, then use that the lcm divides a number exactly when both do; here the translation is carried out by simp with generated private lemmas.

proof_0503.moves: Induct on the natural number n: the base case is exp 0 = 1, and the successor step splits exp((n+1)z) via the addition formula for exp into exp(nz) * exp z, matching pow_succ.

proof_0504.moves: Prove both directions: a covering relation gives the weak covering relation plus distinctness, and conversely a weak covering with distinct endpoints is a covering.
